Israr Ahmad vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 17
May, 2023

Author: Pankaj Bhatia
Bench: Pankaj Bhatia

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc-Lko:34170
Court No. - 17
Case :- Writ - A No. - 3059 of 2023
Petitioner :- Israr Ahmad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. Ganna Chini Udyog Deptt. Lko.

And An
Counsel for Petitioner :- Dinesh Chandra Shukla,Vishal Yadav
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Shireesh Kumar
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Present petition has been filed by the petitioner alleging that the petitioner was a Class - IV employee with the U.P. Co-operative Ganna Samiti Sangh Limited and retired on 31.03.2022.

entities.text: U.P. Co-operative Ganna Samiti Sangh Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is on record that the daughter of the petitioner who was dependent on him met with a serious accident on 24.05.2019 and was hospitalized initially at a hospital known as Kind Hospital, Lucknow and subsequently at different hospitals including a private hospital in the name of Sahara Hospital.

The petitioner claims to have spent an amount of Rs.16,29,082/- on the treatment of the dependent daughter and claimed the amount of compensation spent on the treatment of the daughter mainly on the ground that in terms of the provisions of medical reimbursement rules as amended in the year 2016, the petitioner was entitled for reimbursement of the medical expenses to the extent specified in the said rules.

Israr Ahmad vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99982783/
1 2.

entities.text: Israr Ahmad vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is on record that the daughter of the petitioner also has filed a claim petition under the Motor Vehicle Act, which is pending consideration before the Tribunal and is numbered as MACT No.598 of 2020.

3. In the present petition, the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that on the basis of an application filed by the petitioner, the respondents gave an advance of Rs.2,50,000/- by their sanction letter dated 18.07.2019 (Annexure - 7), however, the other amounts as claimed by the petitioner and spent on the treatment were not given.

The petitioner claims that he had given an undertaking to reimburse the amount as he may get in the claim petition filed on behalf of the daughter of the petitioner; he argues that despite the said undertaking, the amounts as approved by the CMO have not been paid to the petitioner.

4. Learned counsel for the respondents argues that the rules with regard to medical reimbursement payable to the employees of the State Government have been adopted by the respondents on 16.01.2019 and in terms of the incorporation, it is incumbent that the information with regard to the accident is given within 24 hours and an application for approval is also moved within 24 hours.
5. He further draws my attention to an instruction issued to all the Chini Mills Sanghs, including the petitioner, that for taking treatment in the private hospitals, a prior approval is needed.
In the light of the said Government Order dated 16.01.2019, the argument of the respondents is that no prior approval was granted, thus, the amounts are not payable.

6. Considering the mandate of the rules applicable with regard to medical reimbursement and as applicable to the State Government employees and covered by U.P. Government Servants (Medical Attendance)(Second Amendment) Rules, 2016, the amounts are payable.

entities.text: U.P. Government Servants (Medical Attendance)(Second Amendment) Rules, 2016
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The said rules have been adopted by the respondent/corporation and to that extent, there is no issue except that the information with regard to the accident was not given within 24 hours.

7. The first ground taken by the respondents for not paying the amounts that the information was not given within 24 hours cannot be accepted for the sole reason that the respondents themselves,
on an application filed by the petitioner, sanctioned an advance of Rs.2,50,000/- on 18.07.2019 and to that extent, the requirement stood waived by the respondents themselves.

8. As regards the second stand taken in pursuance to the Government Order dated 26.09.2019 to the effect that prior approval is needed, I am of the firm view that the U.P. Co-operative Cane Society and Cane Federation Medical Attendance Rules, have a statutory force and cannot be amended or superseded by a Government Order.

To that extent, the limitation prescribed under the Government Order dated 26.09.2019 cannot be held to be over and above the regulations framed and thus, the second contention on that count is not acceptable.

9. In view of the undertaking given by the petitioner that he will reimburse the amounts received from the Tribunal in pursuance to the application filed by the daughter of the petitioner, I do not see any reason why the amounts are not payable to the petitioner by the respondents in terms of the rules which have been incorporated by the respondent/corporation.

Israr Ahmad vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99982783/
2 10.

entities.text: Israr Ahmad vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the writ petition stands allowed.
11. Respondents are directed to reimburse the amounts as claimed by the petitioner and as approved by the CMO within a period of one month from today.

12. The amounts so given to the petitioner in terms of this order shall be reimbursed by the petitioner as and when the claim petition is decided and if any amount is awarded on the amount spent on medical treatment.

13. Although no prayer with regard to the claim petition has been made, considering the immense hardship faced by the petitioner in the medical treatment incurred, I deem it appropriate to exercise my powers for issuing directions to the Tribunal to hear and decide MACT No.598 of 2020 with all expedition, preferably within a period of four months from today.
